concepts.quote: All zeros, because int / int is integer division. Cast: (double) counts[j] / outDegree gives 0, 0, 0.4, 0.4, 0.2
concepts.why: Applies int truncation to this code (0/5, 2/5, 1/5 all 0) and relates it to the neighbour rule that int op double promotes to a fractional double result.
Writes correct new code that puts the cast on the operand (not the quotient) so the division itself is floating-point, with correct predicted values.
Correctly predicts that moving the point of conversion before the division changes the result from all zeros to the fractional values.

concepts.quote: All zeros, because int / int is integer division ... which sums to 1
concepts.why: Explains that type flow (two int operands) breaks the row, and that the fixed row sums to 1 as a probability distribution requires; it fixes the given failing case rather than reasoning about a class of errors.
